Windows · tray toolkit

Type in the right layout, and keep your text tools one chord away.

The layout marker at the caret and one-key fixes for wrong-layout and CapsLock text work from the first start; a selection menu, a local translator, notes, clipboard history, quick launch and screen capture are one chord away.

A tray toolkit for your keyboard and desktop, for people who type a lot - often in more than one language. Out of the box it shows the active layout next to the caret and fixes text typed in the wrong layout; the optional modules stay off until you switch them on, and by default nothing leaves your computer.

ghbdtn→ Ctrl+Shift+F12 →привет

Start with an ordinary text correction. After launch CyrFlip is already working in the tray; the first step has no destructive action.

Microsoft Store GitHub Releases

The ZIP is not code-signed: extract it to a permanent folder first, for example %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\CyrFlip, and run it from there. Windows warns about the download? What it means and what to click

winget install SerZhyAle.CyrFlip
  1. Install from Microsoft Store, with winget, or extract the ZIP from GitHub Releases to a permanent folder.
  2. Run CyrFlip.exe and find its icon in the notification area.
  3. Select mistyped text and press Ctrl+Shift+F12.

On your first launch, a five-step welcome tour introduces CyrFlip and offers to open Settings on General for initial setup. Skip or close it to keep the defaults. Updates do not show it again; replay it from About. Start with Windows stays off until you choose it.

What CyrFlip does

See the layout before typing

A two-letter marker for any layout appears at the caret; the 13 curated languages have distinct colours, and CapsLock adds a frame. On from the first start.

Fix wrong-layout text and CapsLock

Select text such as ghbdtn and press Ctrl+Shift+F12; add your own layout pairs with a hotkey each, and fix accidental CapsLock with a separate hotkey. Windows keyboard layouts are installed and ordered in the same window.

Act on a selection

Optional: Ctrl and a right click open CyrFlip's own menu at the pointer - copy, convert, fix the case, translate - without losing the selection. The translator runs on a local Ollama model that you install separately. The symbols window finds the character your keyboard lacks by name, keyword or Unicode code and copies it with a click; optional too. Off by default.

Keep what you copy and write

Optional encrypted clipboard history with search and pins, and quick notes on Ctrl+Shift+Alt+N that keep code exactly as typed. Both stay on your computer and move to another one in a plain-text file you export yourself. Off by default.

Launch and capture

Ctrl+F12 puts any screen region on the clipboard, Ctrl+F11 the whole screen, and the Alt variants let you draw on the capture first. Optional Quick launch starts your programs, scripts and yt-dlp downloads from the tray, a hotkey or the taskbar Jump List, and two switches keep the computer awake.

Yours alone

No account, no telemetry, nothing sent to the developer. Optional modules stay off until you switch them on; every hotkey sits in one list where any of them can be reset; 13 interface languages, a light or dark theme, one small program.

Continue with your task

The full guide covers installation, VS Code, and common problems. The privacy policy explains when the keyboard hook, clipboard, and local files are used.

Details and limitations

00Features and settings
  • Any-layout marker at the caret, text cursor, and tray icon; the 13 curated languages have distinct colours, and CapsLock adds a frame around the marker.
  • A conversion table: as many layout ⇄ layout pairs as you like, each with its own hotkey; every pair works both ways and converts by physical key position.
  • A separate hotkey that fixes accidental CapsLock in the selection.
  • A Windows-languages tab: install, reorder and remove layouts, choose the cycle chord, and assign per-language shortcuts that Windows itself handles.
  • An optional menu of CyrFlip's own over the selection: Ctrl and a right click open copying, layout conversion, the case fix and translation right at the pointer, without taking the focus or dropping the selection. Off by default.
  • Optional translation of the selected text by a local Ollama model: Ollama is installed separately and free of charge, the translation appears in a window at the mouse pointer, the directions are an open table with hotkeys of their own, and the result can be copied to the clipboard or pasted over the selection. Off by default; the address is http://localhost:11434 by default - your own computer.
  • Optional clipboard history: search, pin and delete items, pause capture, and Windows DPAPI local encryption.
  • Optional quick notes: Ctrl+Shift+Alt+N opens the window with a new note and the caret already in the body. No Markdown, no highlighting, no auto-formatting - a fragment of code pastes back without a single change; a name is optional, search looks inside the body and the checklist items, and the order is newest first by creation date. There are checklists, export to .txt and Markdown, and a manual transfer to Google Keep through the clipboard. Stored only locally, encrypted with Windows DPAPI, and never collected into the log archive for the author. Off by default.
  • The open exchange file: notes and a chosen part of the clipboard history go to another computer or a phone as one plain UTF-8 text file you export and import yourself - unencrypted on purpose, and the export says so.
  • Screen capture: Ctrl+F12 or the tray item freezes the screen, you drag a region, and the picture goes to the clipboard; Ctrl+F11 takes the whole screen at once, and Ctrl+Alt+F12 and Ctrl+Alt+F11 open a drawing step first: ellipses, rectangles, lines, arrows, an eraser and eight colours. Every capture is also saved as a PNG into a folder of your choice (a switch), which Ctrl+F10 opens while saving is on.
  • An optional Quick launch module (the absorbed OneClickRunner): your programs, scripts and yt-dlp downloads - from the tray, a per-scenario hotkey, and the taskbar Jump List. Off by default.
  • Two keep-awake switches, for the system and for the screen; both are remembered, so one left on keeps the machine awake after a restart too.
  • Per-user autostart, not a Windows service. Interface in 13 languages.
  • A theme for every window, dialog and menu: like Windows (the default), light or dark, switched at once without a restart; Windows high contrast always wins.
  • A searchable settings window: Ctrl+F finds any setting by its name or description, page sections fold away, and the window remembers the open sections, where each page was scrolled, its own size and position, and opens on the monitor you are working on.
  • The Send logs to the author.. button on the About tab packs CyrFlip's own logs into one archive and opens a message to the author with it attached. You send the message yourself, and clipboard history never goes into the archive.
  • On General, export CyrFlip settings to JSON, preview changes before importing, or restore settings before the last import. Three snapshots from before the latest imports stay locally, and a rolling backup of the last three settings states is kept in Documents\CyrFlip\Backups - a fresh install offers to restore it. The file carries chords, tables, switches, traffic-light targets and Quick launch scenarios; it excludes notes, clipboard history, recorded content, credentials and Windows system settings. Enabling history or notes and sending selections to another translation server require separate consent.
01Compatibility and material limitations
Important

Windows 10/11 x64 is required. Profiles convert unambiguous characters by physical key; already composed IME text (such as Chinese Pinyin) is left unchanged.

Some terminals and apps with a custom caret do not expose its position to Windows, so the caret marker may not appear there. In VS Code the external overlay can be imprecise; a companion VS Code extension provides an exact editor marker.

If CyrFlip is force-killed, the system I-beam can remain changed until CyrFlip runs again or you sign in again. Do not run the portable ZIP from a temporary folder: extract it to a permanent place first.

Translation requires Ollama and a language model - a separate free download of several gigabytes that you make once. The quality is the quality of the local model, and the first translation after a cold start takes longer while the model loads; the memory for the model belongs to the Ollama process, not to CyrFlip. Of a long selection the first 4000 characters are translated, and the window says so.

02Privacy, technical information, and releases

The hotkey uses a global keyboard hook; when flipping a selection, the app temporarily uses the clipboard and restores its previous contents. These operations happen locally. Source code, MIT licence, the full privacy note, and release history are available below.

While translation is off, no network connection is opened at all. If you enable it, the selected text is sent over the network to the Ollama address from the settings: by default that is http://localhost:11434 - your own computer, so the text never leaves it. Nothing is sent to the developer or to any cloud service, and the tab says plainly that another address means the text goes to that machine.

03VS Code: an exact marker in the editor

The companion extension reads the layout code published by CyrFlip and draws a marker directly at the VS Code editor caret. The main application must be running; webviews, the terminal, and other non-editor panels cannot host decorations.
